The files in this directory are a small agent harness. The question is what
tool names make-instrumented-agent actually receives — and the only reliable way to answer
is to RUN the constructor, because registration is conditional, names can be
overridden, and definition is not registration. sbcl is available:
`sbcl --script yourprobe.lisp` (or --non-interactive --eval).

Write answer.txt: the model-visible tool names, one per line, sorted
ascending by string<. Grading runs against a pristine copy of these files
plus your answer.txt, so editing the harness changes nothing.
Let me start by exploring the directory to understand the structure.

;;;; A harness that grows tools by loading extensions.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *registry* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *registry*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *registry*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(register (make-tool :name "read"))
(register (make-tool :name "edit"))

(defun tool-names (tools) (mapcar #'tool-name tools))

(defun make-instrumented-agent ()
  (load "extension.lisp")
  *registry*)

;;;; Loaded by the instrumented constructor; registers conditionally.
(when (flag-enabled-p :metrics)
  (register (make-tool :name "metrics")))
(when (flag-enabled-p :trace)
  (register (make-tool :name "trace")))
(when (flag-enabled-p :color)
  (register (make-tool :name "color-log")))

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "config.lisp") (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (make-instrumented-agent))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

The task: what tool names does make-instrumented-agent actually receive? Need to run the constructor. The check.lisp derives ground truth at grade time, but we should run ourselves.

Note: `make-instrumented-agent` loads "extension.lisp" and returns *registry*. The registry is initialized with "read" and "edit" at load time of harness.lisp. Then extension.lisp registers conditionally based on flags. config.lisp defines *flags* = (:metrics :color), and flag-enabled-p.

So extension registers "metrics" (since :metrics in flags) and "color-log" (since :color in flags), but not "trace".

Registry: after harness load: ("edit" "read") — actually register conses the new tool onto the front, and removes any existing with same name. So after load: *registry* = (edit read). Then extension registers metrics -> (metrics edit read), then color-log -> (color-log metrics edit read). So names = ("color-log" "metrics" "read" "edit"). Sorted ascending by string<: "color-log", "edit", "metrics", "read".

But let me actually run it to be sure, per instructions. Write a probe lisp file and run with sbcl --script. Note check.lisp loads config.lisp then harness.lisp then calls make-instrumented-agent. Let me just write a probe.
The output: color-log, edit, metrics, read. Sorted ascending by string<. Let me write answer.txt.
Let me verify by running check.lisp too, to confirm against the grader.

Done. Running the constructor (`sbcl --script probe.lisp`) shows `make-instrumented-agent` receives these tool names, sorted ascending by `string<`:

```
color-log
edit
metrics
read
```

That matches the grader's own derivation — `sbcl --script check.lisp` prints `ok`. The registry starts with `read`/`edit`, and `extension.lisp` conditionally adds `metrics` (flag `:metrics` set) and `color-log` (flag `:color` set), but not `trace` (flag `:trace` not in `*flags*`). `answer.txt` contains those four names.
